exposure: maternal body mass index (BMI) in early pregnancy
cohort: The study included all live singleton females born in Sweden from 1992 through 2002.
finding: The rate of anorexia nervosa decreased with maternal overweight and obesity in a dose-response manner, but sibling control analysis suggested these findings were not consistent with causal effects of maternal BMI on anorexia nervosa in offspring.
followup_time: up to 20 years (from birth year 1992 to diagnosis identification through 2012)
